clue.text: Amount of electricity reduced base volume in equipment

indicators.note: in says the reduced base and the volume sit inside the word for equipment

parts.note: a kit is a set of equipment

indicators.note: reduced tells us to cut the last letter from the synonym for base

parts.note: base in the sense of mean or low-minded gives low

explanation.surface: Someone describes how much power some gear draws after cutting its base volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' is the adjective low (mean), not a foundation; 'reduced' clips its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of electrical potential equal to a thousand volts, so an amount of electricity.

clue.text: Still disappointed with scam, only taken in and in Berlin

indicators.note: taken in says the scam and only words are held inside the German word

parts.note: the German for and is und
a con is a scam or swindle
sole means only, as in the sole survivor

explanation.surface: A victim in Berlin, conned and alone, remains let down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and in Berlin' asks for the German translation of 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has not been comforted remains in their disappointment; still is the adverb here.

clue.text: Scottish bank turned around in near bankruptcy

indicators.note: turned around says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Scottish bank has had to change course when close to going bust.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots a hillside or steep slope is called by this word, so a bank in the landscape sense.

clue.text: Disillusioned youth suffered a failure in power?

definitions.meaning: the young people disenchanted after the First World War, and later cohorts likewise adrift
read literally: the production of electrical power went missing, as in a power cut

explanation.surface: Disaffected young people are blamed for some breakdown in authority.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a cohort of young people left aimless and disenchanted, especially after the Great War.

clue.text: Thread filling megabytes is up still

indicators.note: in a down clue, being up means the whole construction reads from bottom to top
filling means the thread goes inside the megabytes abbreviation

parts.note: MB is the usual abbreviation for megabytes
a lace is a thread or cord, as in a shoelace

explanation.surface: A computing complaint: a thread is clogging memory and something is stuck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is up' turns MLACEB over, as this is a down clue; 'still' is a verb, to calm.
explanation.definitionFit: To make calm or motionless, as wind dropping leaves a sailing ship unable to move; a verb.

clue.text: Maybe Mexican greetings cause alarm

parts.note: hi is a greeting, so several of them are his
to panic people is to cause alarm

explanation.surface: Perhaps a Mexican's hellos are enough to frighten people.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mexican is one example of a person of Spanish-speaking Latin American descent, signalled by 'Maybe'.

clue.text: Apostle follower changes insult to hype during bad management explanation

parts.note: Peter was one of the twelve Apostles

indicators.note: changes ... to says one piece of the follower word is swapped out for another

parts.note: a disciple is a follower
to dis someone is to insult them
PR, public relations, is hype or promotion
in means during, as in in the night

explanation.surface: A disciple of an apostle swaps insult for spin while managing badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes insult to' replaces DIS at the front of DISCIPLE with PR and IN.
explanation.definitionFit: This theory says staff rise until they reach their level of incompetence, explaining poor management.

clue.text: Arnica treated headcases

indicators.note: treated means the letters of the herbal remedy are processed into a new order

explanation.surface: A herbal remedy is used on people who are mentally unhinged.
explanation.definitionFit: Skulls are the cases that hold heads, so read 'headcases' literally rather than as madmen.

clue.text: E.g. Keane gets round individual footballer

indicators.note: gets round says the Irish footballer's first name goes around the other word

parts.note: Roy Keane, the Manchester United captain, is an example of a Roy
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: A footballer such as Keane circles one particular player.
explanation.definitionFit: Wayne, the Manchester United and England striker, bears this surname; a famous player, as with Keane.

clue.text: Extended package features non-binding future with Ferguson, possibly endless rubbish

parts.note: in finance an option is a right, not an obligation, to trade in the future
Alex Ferguson, the Manchester United manager, is one example of an Alex

indicators.note: endless means the last letter of the word for rubbish is dropped

parts.note: trash is rubbish

explanation.surface: A football club's future contract with Ferguson includes add-ons that might be junk.
explanation.definitionFit: Add-ons a buyer may choose on top of the standard package, such as a car's sunroof.

clue.text: Having a bite, eating mashed peeled fruit as healthy food

indicators.note: eating says the eater word takes the next piece inside itself

parts.note: noshing is snacking or eating

indicators.note: mashed means the peeled letters are crushed into a new order
peeled means the skin, first and last letters, comes off the word fruit

explanation.surface: Someone snacks on mashed peeled fruit as a healthy meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peeled' strips the word FRUIT itself to RUI, which 'mashed' shuffles to URI.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is good for you sustains and builds the body; the adjective describes what wholesome food does.

clue.text: Who'd have role in alternative energy?

definitions.text: Who'd have role in alternative energy?

parts.words: Who'd have role in alternative energy?
parts.note: a political group campaigning for renewable power would want a hand in such policy

explanation.definitionFit: This environmentalist political party champions renewables, so it would want a role in alternative energy.

clue.text: Judge barred from prize award

indicators.note: barred from says the judge letter is excluded from the tool word

parts.note: to prize (prise) open is to jemmy, a burglar's crowbar

explanation.surface: A judge has been excluded from a prize-giving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prize' is the verb, to lever open, not a reward.
explanation.definitionFit: The American television industry's statuette for excellence is an award.

clue.text: Personnel breaking cash register tremble

indicators.note: breaking says personnel cuts into the cash register word

parts.note: a till is a cash register
HR, human resources, is the personnel department

explanation.surface: Staff break into the shop till and shake with nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: To quiver with excitement or emotion, a verb sense close to tremble.

clue.text: Interval of rash behaviour getting centre half dismissed

indicators.note: the middle half of the word's letters is sent off, like a defender shown red, leaving the outer quarters

parts.note: recklessness is rash behaviour

explanation.surface: A football break: a centre half is sent off for rash play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre half dismissed' removes the middle six of RECKLESSNESS's twelve letters, KLESSN; 'centre half' is also a football defender.
explanation.definitionFit: A break or pause in proceedings, as when Parliament or a school rises for a time.

clue.text: First of spacemen alone docking moon lander with dignity

indicators.note: First of takes only the opening letter of spacemen
docking says the lander is taken into the word for alone

parts.note: only means alone, as in only child
LEM is the Lunar Excursion Module of the Apollo missions

explanation.surface: An astronaut, alone, docks a lunar module with great composure.
explanation.definitionFit: Done gravely and with ceremony, which is acting with dignity.

clue.text: Plant needing second cull

parts.note: to purge is to cull or get rid of

explanation.surface: A weed that needs a second round of removal.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphorbia is a family of plants with milky sap, commonly known by this name.

clue.text: Courage mostly presented favourably

indicators.note: mostly means the word for courage loses its last letter

parts.note: spunk is courage or pluck

explanation.surface: A display of bravery that was largely given a positive slant.
explanation.definitionFit: Story given a positive slant by a press officer, the participle of the verb to spin.

clue.text: Phlegmatic Conservative kept in check

indicators.note: kept in says the Conservative abbreviation is held inside the check word

parts.note: plaid is a checked tartan cloth

explanation.surface: A calm Tory keeps his emotions in check.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone calm and unexcitable, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Sure to make shallow experience more profound, without any duplicity?

indicators.note: duplicity read as doubling: each doubled letter loses one copy

parts.note: to make something more profound is to deepen it
a dabble is a shallow try at something

explanation.surface: Advice that being reliable means deepening a slight experience, without deceit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make shallow experience more profound' is DEEPEN DABBLE; 'without any duplicity' drops one E from EE and one B from BB.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone you can be sure of is reliable and trustworthy.

clue.text: Version of Alice à la Grimm's supernatural style?

indicators.note: a version of something is a reworking, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A retelling of Alice in the manner of the Brothers Grimm fairy tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Version of' rearranges ALICE A LA GRIMMS.
explanation.definitionFit: A literary mode where fantastical elements appear matter-of-factly in a realistic setting, as in García Márquez.

clue.text: Mounted soldiers note unrestrained style

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means the pieces read upwards

parts.note: OR, other ranks, are ordinary soldiers
fa is the fourth note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Cavalry are recorded as having a free-and-easy look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounted' looks like horsemen but reverses OR FA.
explanation.definitionFit: A rounded, bushy hairstyle left to grow out naturally, so an unrestrained hairdo.

clue.text: Upright member, a Republican, behind tiresome person

indicators.note: behind says the a and Republican pieces come after the tiresome person

parts.note: a pill is a tedious, annoying person

explanation.surface: A worthy politician, a Republican, follows a boring person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upright member' is a vertical structural part, with a nod to an upstanding member of society.
explanation.definitionFit: A vertical column supporting a structure, also a respected stalwart of a community.

clue.text: Confuse powerless mystic symbol

indicators.note: powerless means the letter standing for power is dropped

parts.note: a pentangle is a five-pointed star used in magic

explanation.surface: A magic star that has lost its power baffles people.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the physics symbol for power.
explanation.definitionFit: To tangle up or complicate, making things confused; both are verbs.
